subject: general
question: In which book did Mahatma Gandhi write that the British rule in India was the result of cooperation extended by Indians?

options.text: The Story of My Experiments with Truth

solution:
The correct answer is __**Hind Swaraj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hind Swaraj** is a book written by Mahatma Gandhi in 1909.
 
• In this book, Gandhi critiques modern civilization and lays out his vision for Indian self-rule (Swaraj).
 
• Gandhi argues that British rule in India was possible only because of the cooperation and acceptance by Indians.
 
• He emphasizes the importance of self-reliance and nonviolent resistance to achieve true independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India of My Dreams**

 
 
• This is a book by Mahatma Gandhi that provides a collection of his thoughts and ideas on various aspects of Indian society and its future.
 
• It covers his vision for India's political, social, and economic development.
 
 
 
• **The Story of My Experiments with Truth**
 
 
• This is an autobiography by Mahatma Gandhi, covering his life from early childhood through to 1921.
 
• It details his personal journey and the development of his philosophy of nonviolence (Satyagraha).
 
 
 
• **Village Swaraj**
 
 
• This book comprises writings and speeches by Gandhi on the subject of rural development and the importance of self-sufficient village communities.
 
• Gandhi believed that the foundation of India's development lay in the empowerment of its villages.
